36. A tiling or tessellation of a flat surface is the covering of a plane using one or more geometric
shapes, called tiles, with no overlaps and no gaps. Historically, tessellations were used in
ancient Rome and in Islamic art. You may find tessellation patterns on floors, walls, paintings
etc. Shown below is a tiled floor in the archaeological Museum of Seville, made using
squares, triangles and hexagons.
A craftsman thought of making a floor pattern after being inspired by the above design. To
ensure accuracy in his work, he made the pattern on the Cartesian plane. He used regular
octagons, squares and triangles for his floor tessellation pattern
Use the above figure to answer the question

items.stem: What is the main purpose of weaving mats as described in the passage?
According to the passage, what is a regular pentagon?
What is the key difference between tessellating shapes and other shapes as described in the passage?
In a tiling pattern using triangles and squares, if the triangles are equilateral, how many triangles would fit around a single point?
Which quadrilateral has opposite sides equal and all angles equal to 90 degrees?
If a quadrilateral has all sides equal but angles not equal to 90 degrees, what is it called?
Which shape is formed when two pairs of adjacent sides are equal?
In a circle, if two diameters are drawn and their endpoints are joined, what shape is formed?
If a craftsman uses regular octagons and squares to create a floor pattern, and the pattern requires that each octagon is surrounded by squares, how many squares would fit around one octagon?
If a cube is made of 27 small cubes and painted on the outside, how many small cubes have exactly two faces painted?
If a craftsman uses regular octagons, squares, and triangles to make a tessellation, which shape can be used to fill the space without gaps?
Based on the passage, which of the following is a property of a parallelogram?
Nisha has glued 27 small cubes together to make a large solid cube. She paints the large cube red. How many of the original small cubes have two faces painted red?
In a 3x3x3 cube, how many small cubes have exactly one face painted red?
A student is making a mat using the weaving pattern described in the passage. If the first row follows the pattern '1 under, 1 over, 1 under, 1 over...', what will the second row look like?
A student is trying to create a tessellation pattern using regular pentagons. According to the passage, can regular pentagons fit together around a point without any gaps or overlaps?
A student is creating a tiling pattern using shapes and observes that at certain points, triangles and squares meet. According to the passage, what must be true about the triangles in this pattern?
A student is observing a pattern made with regular octagons and notices that they do not tessellate. According to the passage, what is the reason for this?
A student is creating a tiling pattern with different shapes. According to the passage, what is a requirement for shapes to tessellate?
A student is creating a pattern using a repeating sequence of shapes. If the pattern begins with '2 over, 1 under, 2 over, 1 under...', what will the next part of the pattern be?
Which shape is formed when the four endpoints of two diameters of a circle are joined?
Which of the following is a type of quadrilateral with all sides equal but not all angles equal?
If you want to make a mat with the pattern '1 under, 1 over' for each row, how many rows would you need to complete the pattern if the pattern repeats every two rows?
If a craftsman uses regular octagons, squares, and triangles to make a floor tessellation, which of the following is most likely to be a tile in the design?
